purpose: Distinguish configuration-path/read failure from helper network/configuration-fetch failure without changing behavior or collecting license payloads.
source_qualification: The observed running services and successful TCP connects do not establish a successful helper application protocol exchange.
The manager selected context is not evidence of the helper child context.
Configuration-fetch false flag +0x37c can result from file access or header exchange failures; exit zero does not establish helper success.
Warning-reference hook proves execution reached a warning-string reference, not that a rendered dialog was visible.
Headers returned outside an active fetch are not attributed to that fetch; cross-thread activity needs independent correlation.
identity_guard: Before installing hooks: require main module DEFJobGroupSetup.exe, ia32, pointer size 4, SizeOfImage 1110016.
Read at most expected executable size plus one byte in rb mode, close handle, and require exact file size and SHA-256.
Validate loaded instruction fingerprints at all eight source-bound RVAs; wildcard only relocatable absolute operands.
Any identity exception or mismatch emits probe_identity_rejected and installs zero hooks; never override the guard.
observations: fopen/fclose access summary and matching CreateFileA/W outcomes
IPv4/IPv6 connect endpoint and return status
send/recv requested/returned byte counts without reading buffers
integration_requirements: Orchestrator owns lifecycle and all native captures. Review source before runtime use; this handoff authorizes no competing launch, attach, GUI input or mutable REA database.
Recheck target hash/PID/owned process identity before instrumentation. Do not attach a user-owned helper or reuse a PID without verifying its image and creation context.
Obtain the actual helper command line, parent PID, explicit/inherited CWD and ownership from the process-start capture. Do not invent Run Options inputs from this probe.

For a new bounded diagnostic run, use the existing REA start_frida_session/load_frida_script lifecycle under the orchestrator. Load this file before the helper performs its config fetch if the supported provider lifecycle permits. A late attach cannot prove earlier failures.
Do not acquire GUI input until the supported app-control release/verification prerequisite is resolved. A headless/native observer is not a release workaround.
Require probe_identity_verified and probe_ready before attributing events. Inspect missing_exports_or_hooks and callback errors; a missing required hook makes that observation inconclusive.
Preserve the full raw REA Evidence, process launch identity, script SHA-256, final diagnosticstatus counters if obtainable, observer detach receipt and independent process exit status.
If supported RPC invocation is available, diagnosticstatus reports hook coverage, event counts and dropped events. It is a diagnostic status method, NOT an app-control release operation.

Close the owned Frida session in finally via supported REA close_frida_session. Detachment is not evidence of app-control release. Do not suppress warnings or change return values to complete the run.
Correlate file-access result, active_fetch id, network/24-byte counts, valid flag and warning-reference event. Keep instrumented diagnostic results separate from unmodified GUI acceptance.
Do not rebuild or redeploy reconstructed DEF_PRE_64 v0.2.1 for this diagnostic preparation.
limitations: Prepared and offline tested only; no helper was launched, attached, injected or controlled by this worker.

Frida Interceptor observation changes timing and installs instrumentation in memory, although this script does not edit application arguments, registers, return values, files, configuration or network payloads.
Mocks do not prove installed Frida provider compatibility. API absence is explicitly reported; module exports loaded after installation are not automatically hooked.
File access through another API can evade CreateFile hooks; source-bound fileCheck still records its low-byte summary, not exact fopen errno.
DNS return records do not enumerate all resolved addresses. The endpoint used by connect is separately decoded. Asynchronous ConnectEx/WSASend/WSARecv and other network APIs are outside this probe.

Winsock last_error_snapshot is the hook invocation OS last-error snapshot, not a separately requested WSAGetLastError call; failure return and counts are authoritative observations. A nonblocking pending connect is not final failure.
No network buffer, configuration payload, key, password or full environment is read or logged. Executable bytes are read only for identity hashing.
Exit API entry does not prove actual termination and can be missed after abrupt process death. Exit zero alone is not successful setup.
Event saturation is reported; dropped observations prevent completeness claims. At most eight extra critical events are retained after the ordinary budget.
No GUI, solver, original/reference output comparison or reconstructed-backend acceptance is established by this preparation.

validation.scope: Offline actual-JavaScript mocked-Frida tests and node --check; no app execution
cases: selected context and file handle cleanup
x86 ECX/+0x548 and low return byte
DNS and exact config path filtering
mid-function warning reference uses and executes function callback form

next_ready_task: Orchestrator review of source bindings, observation-only guarantees, hook coverage and tests; runtime diagnosis remains orchestrator-owned and subject to lifecycle gates.

independent_review_repair.finding: warningReference RVA0x4357d is an arbitrary mid-function instruction; generic function-entry onEnter callback object was inappropriate.
independent_review_repair.correction: Added separate instructionProbe that passes a safe function callback to Interceptor.attach at warningReference. Function-entry hooks retain the onEnter/onLeave object form. Identity guard and fingerprint preserved.
independent_review_repair.test: Mock invocation dispatches function callbacks as well as object callbacks. New test asserts callback form, invokes instruction callback and verifies warning-reference evidence with no callback error.
